subject: HealthSpark post-demo: token economics alignment and host benchmarks
messages:

Subject: HealthSpark follow-up: token economics & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Sofia / Jordan —

Thanks for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the follow-ups we promised:

Summary of the workload you described
- Conversational triage + summary assistant for care coordinators
- Typical exchange: ~1.2k tokens prompt (patient + context) + ~300 token response => ~1.5k tokens per interaction on average
- Expected call volume: early pilot 50M interactions/mo equivalent (we mapped this to ~75M tokens/mo), potential scale to 100–200M tokens/mo within 6–12 months depending on adoption

Budget / target pricing notes from the call
- You mentioned procurement levers put an effective target in the low double digits per 1M tokens (roughly $10–$14/1M) to make a migration defensible versus your current vendor economics
- Jordan, you flagged that anything > $18/1M will be hard to justify without a larger contractual commitment

What we promised to deliver
1) Side-by-side $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI / Anthropic / common open-hosts for the same workload (attached)
2) An estimated unit-econ model for HealthSpark at 100M/month with options for caching, quantization, and a Dedicated commit
3) Proposed pilot agreement and a procurement-friendly pricing schedule (30/60/90 day cadence)

Attachments: healthspark_estimate_1m_breakdown.xlsx (unit econ + assumptions), redwood-benchmarks-1m.pdf (quick host comparison)

Next steps / asks
- Please confirm the commit range you can consider for a pilot (50M / 100M / 150M tokens per month) and the procurement timeline (target month to execute PO/MSA)
- If procurement wants a shorter technical review, happy to loop in Vivek for a 30-min ops deep dive

I’ll follow up in ~90 minutes with the benchmark summary from Ben.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Thanks Kim — appreciate the recap. Quick clarifications from our side:  

- We can reasonably consider a 100M tokens/mo commitment for a pilot (staggered: 50M first 30 days then ramp to 100M).
- Procurement has signaled that an effective ceiling for vendor unit cost to be approved is ~$12/1M tokens, unless there are offsets (credits, a multi-year lock, or substantial latency/quality advantages).
- For context, our current spend with Vendor A (OpenAI) averages to about ~$35/1M effective after discounts for the LLMs we run. We know there’s variability by model.

Can Ben/Vivek outline which levers get us closest to the ~$12/1M target for the workload we described (quantization, caching, Dedicated pools, batch sizing)?

Jordan

Subject: RE: HealthSpark follow-up: token economics & next steps (post-demo)

Jordan / Sofia —

Appreciate the clarity on the procurement ceiling. Below is a pragmatic benchmark and a focused levers list tailored to your workload (1.5k tokens/interaction, interactive latency target ~400–600ms).

Quick benchmark (apples-to-apples for 1.5k tokens average) — estimated $/1M (rounded):
- OpenAI (current vendor A, hosted): ~ $35–$40 / 1M (effective, model-dependent)
- Anthropic (hosted): ~ $28–$34 / 1M (effective for Claude-like models)
- Hosted open-model providers (var. quantization, managed): ~ $10–$20 / 1M depending on quant and batching
- Self-host (customer-managed infra, aggressive quantization & batching): ~ $6–$12 / 1M but requires ops + monitoring

Where Redwood lands for HealthSpark (projected at 100M tokens/mo)
- Baseline Hosted Redwood (no commit, typical optimizations): ~$20–$28 / 1M
- Redwood Dedicated (100M commit, quantization + prefix/KV caching + inference optimizations): ~$9–$13 / 1M (we model this with 30–40% effective token reduction from caching + continuous batching gains)

Key levers to hit ~$12/1M:
1) Dedicated capacity with a 12-month reserved profile (predictable throughput + lower per-token kernel pricing)
2) Model quantization to int8 / 4-bit where acceptable — we’ll run quality regression tests on a small eval set (we can keep your safety/quality pass rate as a hard constraint)
3) Smart KV/prefix caching for repeat-context tokens — this is particularly effective in workflows with common patient context blocks and canned system prompts
4) Workload-aware batching (we can tune latency SLOs to trade a small tail-latency increase for better batching efficiency)

Proposed commercial approach (practical starter):
- 3-month pilot: 50M committed first 30 days (discounted token ladder), then step to 100M in month 2 if KPIs met.
- Pilot pricing: target $14/1M effective in month 1 (pilot buffer) with a target $10–$12/1M by month 2 after optimizations and Dedicated placement.
- SLA + rollback policy if latency/quality regressions occur; standard MSA + SOW for pilot period.

I attached the unit-econ spreadsheet with the assumptions (token mix, cache hit rate scenarios, GPU cost ladder). If you want, Vivek and I can run a short technical trial (7–10 days) to validate the quantized latency and the cache hit profile before firming the PO.

Immediate asks from you to make the pilot proposal actionable:
- Confirm whether HealthSpark can sign a 3-month pilot SOW with an initial 50M commit and an internal approval window for ramp to 100M within 30 days.
- Share any procurement T&Cs that are non-negotiable (data residency, SOC2 clause language, insurance limits) and the procurement contact who will review the MSA.

Thanks — Ben
